source_text: ἀληθῶς, ὅταν ἡμῖν ὁ Χριστὸς ἐπιλάμψῃ πάλιν μετὰ τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων ἐν τῇ δόξῃ τοῦ Πατρὸς, τοὺς ἐν καινότητι ζωῆς περιπατεῖν ἑλομένους, καὶ τὸ ἐκπρεπέστατον κάλλος τῆς εὐαγγελικῆς πολιτείας ἐν ὑπομονῇ πλουτήσαντας, παραληψ
pass_a_gloss: …alēthōs… Christos epilampsē… prōtou mēnos / first month… cheimōn apēlthen… deuterō etei / second year… skēnai ou mē seisthōsin…
pass_b_english: Cyril: …truly, when Christ should shine upon us again with the holy angels in the glory of the Father, about to take alongside himself those who have chosen to walk in newness of life, and who have enriched in endurance the most conspicuous beauty of the Gospel way of life, and bringing them into the glory and kingdom long expected. And that a new creation and as it were a new sprout of times and matters belongs to those in Christ, the riddle of the first month would show very well, according to which soft and newly-appearing grasses are on earth, and sprouting-again of plants, and the many-formed beauty of flowers in meadows is shown, of spring laughing fragrance; for somehow in such a time Christ has called the Church from nations, saying thus, ‘Rise, come, my neighbor, my fair one, my dove, because behold the winter has gone away, the rain has gone away, it has traveled in it; the flowers have been seen on the earth; time of cutting has arrived.’ For human nature has sprouted again, as some plant, having been withered by death, both through the transgression in Adam and through the sin that tyrannized over all of us. And I hear Christ saying also through one of the holy prophets, ‘I myself who speak am present, as an hour upon the mountains.’ For what spring works in mountains and thickets, crowning the plants with new sprout, this also our Savior’s presence has fulfilled upon us, having come to be according to times, as in a second year, and not at least in the first time, according to which the law was, and the chorus of the prophets, and according to which death was ruling. For it has reigned from Adam and until Moses. So then as in a second year—that is, as in a time after the first, according to which the law was—the Church from nations has shone up, having Christ as inmate, the end of the prophets and of the law. Does the word seem to you to shoot through toward the straight and true?

Cyril: And I myself think that the more true tent has been announced beforehand for us through Isaiah’s voice, saying as toward each of those called in faith unto righteousness, ‘Your eyes will see Jerusalem, rich cities, tents which will not be shaken, nor will the pegs of its tent be moved; nor will its ropes be torn apart unto the age-long time.’ For the Church is God’s city, of which also all-divine David made mention saying, ‘Glorious things have been spoken concerning you, the city of God.’ For this is rich, and adorned with the gifts from above and from heaven, and having an unbreakable standing in firmness, a seating and remaining. ‘For gates of Hades will not overpower it,’ according to the Savior’s voice.
Palladius: You think most uprightly and fittingly.
Cyril: And when the tent has been raised, that it is fitting for the things in it to lie in order, and not poured-out and carelessly, the Master God of all teaches saying:

choices.why: Spring riddle of Gentile Church call.
